newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Adelaide Bank sees EMTN issue later in year.
newsitem.headline: Adelaide Bank sees EMTN issue later in year.

text.p: Adelaide Bank Ltd said on Tuesday it did not expect to issue paper from its $US750 million Euro medium term note (EMTN) programme until later this year.

Adelaide Bank treasury funding manager Rudy Boeff told Reuters the bank had not needed to launch the programme earlier primarily due to a successful domestic issuance programme done on a tap basis through its domestic transferrable certificates of deposit (TCD) programme.

"We had set (the EMTN programme) in anticipation of future funding requirements and... we found that issuing domestically here in Australia was a cheaper source of funding in the short-term for us," Boeff said.
"So we did that while the opportunity was there and then we will use the EMTN programme sometime in the future," he said, adding that while a date had not been set, it would be later this year.
Boeff said the bank also had no immediate plans for a second mortgage securitisation tranche under its Torrens Trust programme.
The bank last year revealed plans for a further A$200 million tranche timed for April or May of this year.
However, Boeff said there were no plans to proceed in the short-term.
"We have just done a A$40 million capital notes issue so we do not need to securitise at this time ... but there should be something planned within the next 12 months," he said.
